title: Poppy and the Wobbly Dream
markdown:
Poppy the puppy loved sunshine and soft naps. Her tail wagged like a happy little flag, and her ears were as floppy as two warm pancakes. Her favourite place was her own sunny garden. Daisies nodded hello there, and ladybugs wore shiny red coats. It smelled of roses and yummy dirt after a drink of water. Every little stone and every blade of grass felt like home.

With Poppy, always, was Nim. Nim was a moon moth, soft and shimmery like starlight. His wings pulsed gently, like a quiet breath, leaving faint sparkles. He smelled like moonlight and sweet dew. Poppy and Nim were the very best of friends, exploring every tiny flower and chasing every playful breeze together.

Poppy liked things to be just so. She liked paths that stayed still and grass that did not wiggle too much. If things started to jiggle or wobble, like jelly on a plate or a bouncy patch of grass, her little paws would feel very still, and her tail would tuck right underneath her. Her tummy would feel funny, as if it had borrowed a ripple from a pond.

One afternoon, the sun began to paint the sky with sleepy colours. A tiny sound drifted from the old oak tree. It was a little baby bird, peeking from its nest. “My dream. My dream is gone,” it chirped. Floating away on the breeze was a soft pearly bubble. Inside it was the baby bird’s special dream of flying high over fluffy clouds. If the bubble floated away, the baby bird would not have his sweet dream to whisper when he slept.

“Oh dear,” woofed Poppy, her ears perking up. “A lost dream. We must help.” Her tail gave a small uncertain wag. The bubble bobbed on the breeze, swaying this way and that. It looked a little wobbly. Poppy’s paws felt heavy. She almost wished she was snuggled in her soft bed, safe and still, with the daisies doing all the nodding.

Nim, with his calm silvery glow, landed gently on Poppy’s nose. His touch was as light as a falling leaf. “The dream is important. And we are together.” He knew Poppy liked things to be predictable. He also knew how far they had already walked as friends. “We must go after it. Before it floats too far.” The baby bird’s sleepy chirps encouraged them. A single down-feather drifted from the nest and stuck to Poppy’s ear like a tiny flag of its own.

With a brave little hop, Poppy decided to go. They left their familiar garden and tiptoed toward the edge of the Whispering Woods. The woods were not dark or scary. The trees were tall and friendly, their leaves rustling like secrets. The air smelled of damp earth and pine needles, a new and interesting smell. Everything felt bigger, and the path had dancing shadows that made Poppy’s tummy flutter.

Their first challenge was a patch of moon-grass. It was soft and silvery, like Nim’s own wings, and it tickled. As they walked, the grass bent and swayed, making little waves that whispered against their legs. Poppy’s paws felt a little unsure, sinking slightly into the soft blades. “It tickles so much,” she giggled, a happy giggle, but her tail gave a nervous flick. Nim flew just ahead, his light a steady lamp showing her where to step. A cricket hopped aside as if this were a regular crossing.

Soon they came to a little stream. The water flowed with a cheerful gurgle, and tiny ripples bounced over smooth stones. Poppy stopped. Her legs felt like soft pudding. The stream looked very, very wobbly. She remembered the dream bubble, still floating ahead, its pearly shimmer a faint beacon. She remembered the sad little baby bird. She squeezed her eyes shut for a moment. She needed to be careful. She almost wanted to turn back.

Nim fluttered down and nudged her ear. “One step at a time, Poppy. Just one wobbly step.” She took a deep breath, the scent of damp earth filling her lungs. With Nim beside her, a steady shimmering friend, she carefully stepped onto the first bobbing stone. And then another. And then another. She found that if she watched Nim’s light and took steady breaths, the wobbling was not so tricky after all. It was just water dancing. A minnow flicked under the third stone, silver as Nim’s wing.

And there it was. The dream bubble, shimmering like a tiny rainbow, had landed on a fluffy round dandelion. The dandelion swayed in the breeze, its seeds like tiny parachutes. It was beautiful, and so wobbly. The bubble sat right in the middle. Poppy hesitated. The idea of stepping onto something so soft and airy made her paws tingle. She felt the tickly dry texture of the dandelion’s stem against her nose as she leaned in. She heard the soft rustle of its many seeds. She saw its gentle sway against the blue sky.

With a determined little huff, Poppy put one paw, then another, carefully, gently, onto the fluffy head of the dandelion. It dipped and wobbled, a shy sway, but she held her balance, remembering the stream. She felt the fluff tickle her paws. Then, with a soft puff of air, the bubble gently detached itself.

Nim carefully guided the dream bubble toward Poppy. She scooped it up in her soft mouth, holding it as gently as she could. It felt like holding a warm happy secret. They made their way back. The wobbly stream no longer seemed so tricky, and the tickly grass was just a pleasant tickle. A stone she had feared on the way out now felt like a friend with a wet back. They returned to the old oak tree. With a soft puff, Poppy released the bubble right back to the baby bird. The baby bird chirped with joy, its little eyes shining. “Thank you, Poppy. Thank you, Nim. My dream is safe.”

As Poppy and Nim walked back into their garden, the setting sun warmed their fur. The garden still smelled of daisies and sunshine. Something felt different. Poppy trotted past a patch of slightly bumpy ground. Instead of her paws feeling still, she felt a quiet confidence, a warm glow. She even nudged a wobbly-looking daisy with her nose, and it seemed to giggle, its petals dancing. She lay down in the soft grass, her tail giving a contented thump-thump against the earth, and watched the stars begin to twinkle, just like Nim’s wings, in the velvet sky. The baby bird, in the oak, whispered its cloud-dream, and Poppy’s ears stayed floppy and unafraid.
